update_mem_hiwater has attracted various criticisms
concerned with mm scalability.  Originally it was called whenever rss or
total_vm got raised.  Then many of those callsites were replaced by a timer
tick call from account_system_time.  Now Frank van Maarseveen reports that to
be found inadequate.  How about this?  Works for Frank.
Replace update_mem_hiwater
column2: a poor combination of two unrelated ops

column1: update_hiwater_rss and update_hiwater_vm.  Don't attempt to keep
mm->hiwater_rss up to date at timer tick
column2: nor every time we raise rss (usually

column1: by 1): those are hot paths.  Do the opposite
column2: update only when about to lower

column1: rss (usually by many)
column2: or just before final accounting in do_exit.  Handle

column1: mm->hiwater_vm in the same way
column2: though it's much less of an issue.  Demand

column1: that whoever collects these hiwater statistics do the work of taking the
maximum with rss or total_vm.
And there has been no collector of these hiwater statistics in the tree.  The
new convention needs an example
column2: so match Frank's usage by adding a VmPeak

column1: line above VmSize to /proc/<pid>/status
column2: and also a VmHWM line above VmRSS

column1: (High-Water-Mark or High-Water-Memory).
There was a particular anomaly during mremap move
captured too high.  A fleeting such anomaly remains
corrected now
What locking?  None: if the app is racy then these statistics will be racy
it's not worth any overhead to make them exact.  But whenever it suits
hiwater_vm is updated under exclusive mmap_sem
page_table_lock (for now) or with preemption disabled (later on): without
going to any trouble
column2: minimize the time between reading current values and

column1: updating
column2: to minimize those occasions when a racing thread bumps a count up

column1: and back down in between.
